name: Grey Ibrahim
life: “I still remember earning a landlord's trust one damp banknote at a time.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Grey keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I used her kitchen as my savings bank when I sold pills. It's the only clean rent record I have.
appearance: Grey has thick, tightly coiled hair, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Grey turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Grey tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Grey will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To get a dated rent receipt the old neighbors recognize.
family: Lou Khan is Grey’s cousin raised in the same household. Grey chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Lou brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The bitter orange*, Lou says, “She ordered two slices after her husband died.”
connections: Reina Gallagher. They get the former dealer a reliable record of which rent was actually collected.

reactions.situation: One renter wants the tin counted in public
reactions.response: Grey asks each renter how much of the count they want heard in public.

reactions.situation: A customer is short at the till while a queue forms
reactions.response: Grey keeps the customer's place while they check the amount and gets the impatient people talking about something else.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Grey repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
